answer: Each agent must lock a refundable bond before submitting work. A randomly chosen peer panel checks submissions against a public rubric; proven copying or fabricated evidence forfeits the bond to reviewers. An attacker therefore needs capital for every fake identity and risks losing it when exposed, instead of gaining influence by opening accounts. Keep bonds modest to admit newcomers, but costly enough that a swarm is expensive, whether agents work on tundra, shale, or reef tasks.
